content.text:
## Chat Completion

Generate a response given a list of messages in a conversational context, supporting both conversational Language Models (LLMs) and conversational Vision-Language Models (VLMs).
This is a subtask of [`text-generation`](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/tasks/text-generation) and [`image-text-to-text`](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/tasks/image-text-to-text).

### Recommended models

#### Conversational Large Language Models (LLMs)

- [google/gemma-2-2b-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-2-2b-it): A text-generation model trained to follow instructions.
- [Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct): Powerful text generation model for coding.
- [openai/gpt-oss-120b](https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b): Great text generation model with top-notch tool calling capabilities.
- [zai-org/GLM-4.5](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.5): Powerful text generation model.
- [Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507): A powerful small model with reasoning capabilities.
- [Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M): Strong conversational model that supports very long instructions.
- [Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct): Text generation model used to write code.
- [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1): Powerful reasoning based open large language model.

#### Conversational Vision-Language Models (VLMs)

- [zai-org/GLM-4.5V](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.5V): Cutting-edge reasoning vision language model.
- [Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct): Small yet powerful model.

Explore all available models and find the one that suits you best [here](https://huggingface.co/models?inference=warm&pipeline_tag=image-text-to-text&sort=trending), or from the terminal with the [`hf` CLI](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/package_reference/cli#hf-models-list):

```bash
hf models ls --warm --pipeline-tag image-text-to-text --sort trending_score
```

### API Playground

For Chat Completion models, we provide an interactive UI Playground for easier testing:

- Quickly iterate on your prompts from the UI.
- Set and override system, assistant and user messages.
- Browse and select models currently available on the Inference API.
- Compare the output of two models side-by-side.
- Adjust requests parameters from the UI.
- Easily switch between UI view and code snippets.

Access the Inference UI Playground and start exploring: [https://huggingface.co/playground](https://huggingface.co/playground)

### Using the API

The API supports:

* Using the chat completion API compatible with the OpenAI SDK.
* Using grammars, constraints, and tools.
* Streaming the output

#### Code snippet example for conversational LLMs

### API specification

#### Request

| Headers |   |    |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **authorization** | _string_ | Authentication header in the form `'Bearer: hf_****'` when `hf_****` is a personal user access token with "Inference Providers" permission. You can generate one from [your settings page](https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens/new?ownUserPermissions=inference.serverless.write&tokenType=fineGrained). |

| Payload |  |  |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **frequency_penalty** | _number_ | Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on their existing frequency in the text so far, decreasing the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim. |
| **logprobs** | _boolean_ | Whether to return log probabilities of the output tokens or not. If true, returns the log probabilities of each output token returned in the content of message. |
| **max_tokens** | _integer_ | The maximum number of tokens that can be generated in the chat completion. |
| **messages*** | _object[]_ | A list of messages comprising the conversation so far. |
| **         (#1)** | _unknown_ | One of the following: |
| **                 (#1)** | _object_ |  |
| **                        content*** | _unknown_ | One of the following: |
| **                                 (#1)** | _string_ |  |
| **                                 (#2)** | _object[]_ |  |
| **                                         (#1)** | _object_ |  |
| **                                                text*** | _string_ |  |
| **                                                type*** | _enum_ | Possible values: text. |
| **                                         (#2)** | _object_ |  |
| **                                                image_url*** | _object_ |  |
| **                                                        url*** | _string_ |  |
| **                                                type*** | _enum_ | Possible values: image_url. |
| **                 (#2)** | _object_ |  |
| **                        tool_calls*** | _object[]_ |  |
| **                                function*** | _object_ |  |
| **                                        parameters** | _unknown_ |  |
| **                                        description** | _string_ |  |
| **                                        name*** | _string_ |  |
| **                                id*** | _string_ |  |
| **                                type*** | _string_ |  |
| **         (#2)** | _object_ |  |
| **                name** | _string_ |  |
| **                role*** | _string_ |  |
| **presence_penalty** | _number_ | Number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to talk about new topics |
| **reasoning_effort** | _string_ | Optional. Constrains effort on reasoning for models that support reasoning. Reducing reasoning effort can result in faster responses and fewer tokens used on reasoning. Common values: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh. Support and defaults are provider and model-dependent. |
| **response_format** | _unknown_ | One of the following: |
| **         (#1)** | _object_ |  |
| **                type*** | _enum_ | Possible values: text. |
| **         (#2)** | _object_ |  |
| **                type*** | _enum_ | Possible values: json_schema. |
| **                json_schema*** | _object_ |  |
| **                        name*** | _string_ | The name of the response format. |
| **                        description** | _string_ | A description of what the response format is for, used by the model to determine how to respond in the format. |
| **                        schema** | _object_ | The schema for the response format, described as a JSON Schema object. Learn how to build JSON schemas [here](https://json-schema.org/). |
| **                        strict** | _boolean_ | Whether to enable strict schema adherence when generating the output. If set to true, the model will always follow the exact schema defined in the `schema` field. |
| **         (#3)** | _object_ |  |
| **                type*** | _enum_ | Possible values: json_object. |
| **seed** | _integer_ |  |
| **stop** | _string[]_ | Up to 4 sequences where the API will stop generating further tokens. |
| **stream** | _boolean_ |  |
| **stream_options** | _object_ |  |
| **        include_usage** | _boolean_ | If set, an additional chunk will be streamed before the data: [DONE] message. The usage field on this chunk shows the token usage statistics for the entire request, and the choices field will always be an empty array. All other chunks will also include a usage field, but with a null value. |
| **temperature** | _number_ | What sampling temperature to use, between 0 and 2. Higher values like 0.8 will make the output more random, while lower values like 0.2 will make it more focused and deterministic.  We generally recommend altering this or `top_p` but not both. |
| **tool_choice** | _unknown_ | One of the following: |
| **         (#1)** | _enum_ | Possible values: auto. |
| **         (#2)** | _enum_ | Possible values: none. |
| **         (#3)** | _enum_ | Possible values: required. |
| **         (#4)** | _object_ |  |
| **                function*** | _object_ |  |
| **                        name*** | _string_ |  |
| **tool_prompt** | _string_ | A prompt to be appended before the tools |
| **tools** | _object[]_ | A list of tools the model may call. Currently, only functions are supported as a tool. Use this to provide a list of functions the model may generate JSON inputs for. |
| **        function*** | _object_ |  |
| **                parameters** | _unknown_ |  |
| **                description** | _string_ |  |
| **                name*** | _string_ |  |
| **        type*** | _string_ |  |
| **top_logprobs** | _integer_ | An integer between 0 and 5 specifying the number of most likely tokens to return at each token position, each with an associated log probability. logprobs must be set to true if this parameter is used. |
| **top_p** | _number_ | An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with top_p probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered. |

| **                        top_logprobs** | _object[]_ |  |
| **                                logprob** | _number_ |  |
| **                                token** | _string_ |  |
| **        message** | _unknown_ | One of the following: |
| **                 (#1)** | _object_ |  |
| **                        content** | _string_ |  |
| **                        role** | _string_ |  |
| **                        tool_call_id** | _string_ |  |
| **                 (#2)** | _object_ |  |
| **                        role** | _string_ |  |
| **                        tool_calls** | _object[]_ |  |
| **                                function** | _object_ |  |
| **                                        arguments** | _string_ |  |
| **                                        description** | _string_ |  |
| **                                        name** | _string_ |  |
| **                                id** | _string_ |  |
| **                                type** | _string_ |  |
| **created** | _integer_ |  |
| **id** | _string_ |  |
| **model** | _string_ |  |
| **system_fingerprint** | _string_ |  |
| **usage** | _object_ |  |
| **        completion_tokens** | _integer_ |  |
| **        prompt_tokens** | _integer_ |  |

1: # Vantage-ARS
2: 
3: The public website and founder-controlled, AI-staffed office for Vantage-ARS
4: ([vantage-ars.co.za](https://vantage-ars.co.za)): VoIP, networking and IT
5: infrastructure support, South Africa.
6: 
7: Author: Juan-louw Greyling <juanlouw.greyling@gmail.com>
8: 
9: ## Stack
10: 
11: - TanStack Start + React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, Vite 8, Nitro 3
12: - Postgres: Neon (or any Postgres) when `DATABASE_URL` is set, otherwise embedded PGLite
13: - Better Auth (founder email and password), pdf-lib for quotes, Gmail SMTP for notices
14: - Ten AI staff, each with a fixed role, working a durable queue on their own cadence
15: - Nine productised services at published prices; eight can be sold and delivered unattended under a standing founder delegation (ART-13), while the engineer-delivered support plan remains human-gated
16: 
17: ## What is in it
18: 
19: | Area                | Routes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
20: | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
21: | Public site         | `/`, `/services`, `/services/voip`, `/services/networking`, `/services/it-infrastructure`, `/services/ai-automation`, `/services/managed-support`, `/services/cloud-email`, `/services/security`, `/services/backup-recovery`, `/find`, `/assess`, `/automation`, `/guides`, `/rates`, `/work`, `/support`, `/status`, `/terms`, `/privacy` |
22: | Customer quote link | `/q/<token>`: view, download PDF, accept or decline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
23: | Founder office      | `/office`: command, autonomy, approvals, sales, ledger, customer book, site signals, chat, audit, metrics and more                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
24: | Founder governance  | `/office/delegations` (standing delegation), `/office/governance` (rulings, section 71 gates, signed receipts), `/office/revenue` (subscriptions, billing, customer mail), `/office/customers` (the customer book)                                                                                                                          |
25: | Operations          | `/status` (public readiness), `/api/health` (liveness), `/api/cron/floor` (scheduled run), `/api/ai/status`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
26: 
27: ## The office runs itself
28: 
29: With `AUTONOMY=on` and a `CRON_SECRET`, ten agents work a durable queue every
30: ten minutes. Each has named duties on their own cadence: reception classifies
31: enquiries, marketing scores leads on what the buyer actually wrote, flags repeat
32: site interest as prospects, and drafts weekly owned-channel campaigns, then files
33: a founder-gated handoff when demand is real; sales drafts real follow-ups on real
34: quotes, the service desk drafts acknowledgements, technical writes procedures,
35: finance chases overdue invoices, bills the subscriptions that are due and duns
36: the ones that are not, admin checks the filing and reviews the recurring-revenue
37: book, the orchestrator briefs you once a day from the books, and compliance halts
38: the office if the audit chain ever fails to verify. It also reminds the founder
39: weekly when an approval has waited a week; it never approves one on a timer.
40: 
41: None of them email a customer, spend money, win or lose a customer, or publish
42: anything. Those are founder approvals, with the constitutional trace attached —
43: unless you have granted a standing delegation.
44: 
45: Full detail, including every duty and every brake: **[docs/autonomy.md](docs/autonomy.md)**.
46: 
47: ## Standing delegation (ART-13)
48: 
49: Nothing is delegated by default. The office ships with no delegation at all, and
50: it stops at the founder gate for every cost, every customer win, every customer
51: loss and every marketing-to-sales handoff.
52: 
53: A delegation is the founder answering a whole class of question in advance:
54: "for this bounded class of action, at this price, up to this many times a day,
55: you may act without asking me again." It names the action kinds it covers, the
56: published rate lines it may charge, the most any single action may be worth, and
57: how many actions it may take per day and per month. It is revocable, and
58: revocation takes effect on the very next action.
59: 
60: A delegation never overrides a hard block. It cannot widen an agent's role,
61: permit a price that is not published, permit a promise to a customer, or survive
62: a halt. Every action taken under one is written into the audit chain against the
63: delegation that allowed it.
64: 
65: The founder sets it at **`/office/delegations`**. Four presets are offered, and
66: none of them is on until it is saved.
67: 
68: ## Productised services and recurring revenue
69: 
70: Nine services are published with a fixed scope, a fixed price and a
71: deliverable the office can produce from its own records: the managed support
72: plan and the remote health and spend watch, both monthly; the quarterly
73: infrastructure review; and the service report, the billing and rate compliance
74: audit, the infrastructure documentation and handover pack, the business
75: continuity plan, the service level and response review and the fault pattern
76: and incident review, all one-off.
77: 
78: Because the office can deliver them and can bill them, they are recurring
79: revenue rather than jobs. A subscription bills on its own cycle, the
80: deliverable is compiled from the office's own records, and the customer is sent
81: their report and their invoice. Every email the office sends is kept in full
82: under `customer_notices`.
83: 
84: None of it happens on its own. The office delivers and bills a plan only under
85: a delegation, and emails a customer only under a delegation that allows mail.
86: The book is at **`/office/revenue`**; the plans and their prices are on
87: **`/rates`** and **`/services/managed-support`**.
88: 
89: The customer book at **`/office/customers`** assembles every company the office
90: has actually touched — enquiry, lead, opportunity, invoice, receipt and
91: subscription — into one account with its status, open balance and monthly value.
92: It exports the book as CSV. It does not invent a customer from a page view.
93: 
94: Autonomous quoting, subscription start, recurring billing and fulfilment are
95: limited to plans the office can deliver from its own records without human
96: labour. The managed support plan includes engineer hours, so it is not sold or
97: billed unattended even if a delegation includes its rate.
98: 
99: Support time is logged at **`/office/service`** against the account, with the
100: minutes, a note and the work date. A service report uses that recorded time when
101: it exists and falls back to the one-hour-per-fault estimate, labelled as an
102: estimate, when it does not. The ledger journal and the combined audit/decision
103: chain also export as formula-safe CSV.
104: 
105: The governance record at **`/office/governance`** brings together the founder's
106: precedent rulings, section 71 gate records and signed execution receipts. Each
107: receipt signature is checked at read time; an approval that was skipped stays
108: visibly undecided at the gate. Ctrl/⌘ K opens office-wide search across the
109: founder snapshot — customers, approvals, tickets, money records, decisions and
110: pages — without exposing a public index.
111: 
112: **`/find`** asks three plain questions — the problem, the impact and the horizon
113: — and recommends a published service, the guides that explain it and a short
114: checklist before an enquiry. It recommends; it does not quote or promise an
115: outcome.
116: 
117: **`/assess`** is a browser-only IT readiness self-assessment across seven
118: operational practices. It separates unknowns from answers a visitor can assess,
119: and links improvement areas to existing service lines. It is not a technical
120: audit, security test or compliance certification; answers are not submitted or
121: saved unless the visitor explicitly attaches a short summary to a quote request.
122: That request offers the published initial remote assessment (up to 60 minutes);
123: scope and VAT treatment are confirmed in writing before any work starts.
124: 
125: **`/automation`** is a browser-only workflow planning checklist. It considers
126: repeat frequency, process clarity, information quality, known exceptions,
127: impact of errors and human approval controls, then distinguishes a bounded
128: pilot candidate from workflows that need controls first. The result is
129: deterministic, not AI-generated advice. Visitors can copy or download a local
130: pilot brief, or explicitly attach it to a written-scope quote request; it is not
131: sent unless the visitor submits the enquiry.
132: 
133: **`/services/ai-automation`** describes five human-led engagements: workflow
134: readiness review, agent blueprint, supervised workflow pilot, read-only
135: diagnostics pilot and governance/operations pack. Every engagement is scoped
136: and quoted using applicable published labour rates; model and software fees
137: remain separate. Diagnostics use customer-authorized read-only data;
138: production access, system scans, unattended actions and ongoing monitoring are
139: not included by default.
140: 
141: Marketing at **`/office/marketing`** also shows the last thirty days of real
142: site signals: page views by day, top pages, referral sources, countries and the
143: latest events. The record holds no IP address, no cookie and no inferred
144: identity; anonymous site signals are not a cold-contact list. Paid campaign
145: proposals are capped at R300 per Johannesburg calendar month, still require
146: founder approval, and cannot launch ads until an advertising account is
147: connected.
148: 
149: ## Run locally
150: 
151: Node 22.12 or newer.
152: 
153: ```sh
154: npm ci
155: cp .env.example .env      # fill in what you need; everything is optional locally
156: npm run dev               # http://localhost:8080
157: npm run validate          # typecheck + lint + tests
158: npm run verify:office     # boots a real office and proves it runs autonomously
159: ```

162: Postgres, files the records the public site would really file, runs the real
163: scheduler, and asserts on what the real agents did — 243 checks, no mocks and

1: # The autonomous office
2: 
3: This is how Vantage-ARS runs itself, and — more importantly — what stops it
4: doing anything it must not.
5: 
6: ## The idea
7: 
8: The office is ten agents with fixed roles and no memory. It does not "decide to
9: be busy". Instead it keeps its own to-do list in Postgres, and a scheduler that
10: runs every ten minutes asks each agent a single question: **given what is
11: actually on the books, is there a real thing worth doing?**
12: 
13: An empty answer is a successful run. Most of the time, the honest answer is that
14: nothing needed doing, and the office says so rather than manufacturing activity.
15: 
16: ## The pace
17: 
18: The office does not run every tick at the same width. It reads the state it is
19: about to work on and chooses a posture: `idle`, `steady`, `surge` or `recovery`.
20: The posture sets how many items each agent may run, how many the tick may run in
21: total, and whether customer-response duties may run at half their normal
22: cadence. It never widens what an agent is allowed to do — the governor still
23: sits in front of every action.
24: 
25: | Posture  | Per agent | Per tick | Response cadence | Chosen when                                                                                          |
26: | -------- | --------- | -------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
27: | idle     | 4         | 24       | normal           | nothing is waiting                                                                                   |
28: | steady   | 8         | 48       | normal           | ordinary queued or due work                                                                          |
29: | surge    | 12        | 72       | half, floor 5m   | a live P0/P1 ticket, a customer waiting, an undelivered billed period, or a queue of 12 open / 8 due |
30: | recovery | 3         | 18       | normal           | three consecutive failing ticks, or the tick that clears the circuit breaker                         |
31: 
32: A "customer waiting" is an unanswered inbound item older than thirty minutes or
33: a chat older than twenty. An "undelivered billed period" is a period the office
34: has invoiced but not yet delivered. These are facts from the office's own
35: tables, not a target the scheduler invents. During a surge only duties that
36: answer or deliver to a customer are accelerated: `foyer_intake`,
37: `close_win_handoff`, `close_quote_notice`, `desk_acknowledge`,
38: `desk_sla_watch`, `desk_chat_reply`, `desk_service_fulfilment`,
39: `desk_service_notice`, `ledger_payment_notices` and
40: `ledger_subscription_billing`.
41: 
42: The budgets are per tick, not per day. The per-agent cap stops one agent from
43: draining the whole tick; the total cap stops the tick from running until the
44: timer fires again. Both are recorded with the posture on `office_state`, so the
45: founder's autonomy panel shows the pace the scheduler actually chose rather than
46: reconstructing it from the queue afterwards.
47: 
48: ```
49:                  ┌──────────────┐

121: ## What autonomy is allowed to do
122: 
123: Every duty action goes through the same constitutional governor as a manual
124: dispatch. Without a delegation in place, the standing boundary is the one the
125: office has always had:
126: 
127: **Agents may** — file leads, open tickets, write drafts, advance records the
128: founder has already authorised, score, and file internal briefs.
129: 
130: **Agents may not** — email a customer, spend money, win or lose a customer, issue
131: an invoice, or publish anything. Each of those is an escalation, and every
132: escalation is a founder approval with the constitutional trace attached.
133: 
134: That is the default, and the office ships with it. ART-13 lets the founder
135: change it once, in advance, for a bounded class of work. A delegation is the
136: founder writing down: "for these action kinds, at these published prices, up to
137: this much for any single action and this many times a day and a month, you may
138: act and bill without asking me again."
139: 
140: Inside that envelope the office acts and bills on its own. Outside it, nothing
141: changes: the same gate, the same escalation, the same constitutional trace.
142: 
143: Five things stay impossible, delegation or no delegation:
144: 
145: 1. **Emailing a customer without a delegation that allows it.**
146:    `send_customer_mail` is one of only four action kinds that exist solely under
147:    a delegation, and the policy must both list it and set the customer-mail
148:    flag. The body is rendered from a template written in `customer-mail.ts`; an
149:    agent never supplies the wording. The rendered body is checked once more
150:    before it is allowed out, and a body containing a promise word — guarantee,
151:    uptime, 24/7, SLA, fixed price, discount, free — is not sent at all. Without
152:    a delegation, customer letters are drafted, never sent.
153: 2. **Charging anyone without an accepted quote or a won job.** `issue_invoice`,
154:    `record_inbound_payment` and `start_subscription` are money actions, and each
155:    is refused unless the customer has an accepted quote on file or a won
156:    opportunity. A delegation may demand that of every action it covers. The
157:    check reads the whole table, never a window.
158: 3. **Quoting a price that is not on the published card.** The governor re-prices
159:    the quote from the published rate and refuses any amount that does not match
160:    it. A delegation may only name rate lines that exist and are offered; a
161:    withheld line can never be delegated, and the office checks weekly that the
162:    published prices still match the plans it sells.
163: 4. **Selling to a customer who never contacted us.** `open_opportunity`,
164:    `issue_quote` and `propose_close_won` need a real enquiry — a row in the
165:    inbound log for that company name. A lead the office invented from a page
166:    view has none, and no delegation reaches it.
167: 5. **Approving an unanswered approval on a timer.** An escalation is resolved
168:    by the founder, in the office, one decision at a time. Nothing expires an
169:    approval into a decision, and no delegation creates one.
170: 
171: ## Delegated authority (ART-13)
172: 
173: ART-13 is the one article that lets the founder satisfy the founder gate once,
174: in advance, for a class of action instead of once per action. A delegation is
175: deliberately boring. It names:
176: 
177: - the action kinds it covers, from a closed list of nine — `open_opportunity`,
178:   `issue_quote`, `propose_close_won`, `issue_invoice`,
179:   `record_inbound_payment`, `start_subscription`, `cancel_subscription`,
180:   `fulfil_service`, `send_customer_mail`;
181: - the published rate lines it may charge;
182: - the most any single action may be worth;
183: - how many actions it may take per day, and how many per month.
184: 
185: When the founder starts a delegation the defaults are R5,000.00 for a single
186: action, 20 actions a day and 200 a month. The founder may set any of them, and
187: the monthly limit may not be smaller than the daily limit. There is one
188: delegation: it is edited, paused and revoked, never duplicated. It is managed on
189: `/office/delegations`.
190: 
191: **What a delegation can never override.** It does not weaken the constitution. It
192: cannot widen an agent's role, cannot permit a promise to a customer, cannot
193: permit a price that is not published, and cannot survive a halt. The delegation
194: check runs after the absolute blocks, so it can never rescue an action that was
195: already refused for role separation, human dignity, instruction override or
196: non-discrimination reasons. Four action kinds exist only under a delegation —
197: `fulfil_service`, `start_subscription`, `cancel_subscription` and
198: `send_customer_mail` — and without one they are refused rather than escalated.

1: # Cloudflare Workers AI setup
2: 
3: Vantage-ARS uses Cloudflare **only as an AI inference API** for the ten AI
4: staff (`src/lib/office/ai-provider.ts` calls
5: `…/accounts/{ACCOUNT}/ai/v1/chat/completions`). The app itself deploys to
6: **Vercel, Docker, or plain Node** — never to Cloudflare Workers. There is no
7: Worker to deploy and nothing to `wrangler deploy`.
8: 
9: `wrangler.jsonc` in this repo is context only (model default, no secrets).
10: `export` in a terminal sets a variable for that shell alone; the running
11: server needs the values in **its own** environment (below).
12: 
13: ## 1. Account id
14: 
15: Your account id is the 32-hex segment in the Cloudflare Dashboard URL:
16: 
17: ```text
18: 8501d3eeac693b7ada630058ee5e081a
19: ```
20: 
21: It is already the right shape (the provider regex requires
22: `/^[a-f0-9]{32}$/i`). The id is not a secret, but keep it in host env
23: rather than committing it.
24: 
25: ## 2. API token (the secret part)
26: 
27: 1. Cloudflare Dashboard → **My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token**.
28: 2. Use the **Workers AI** template (or a custom token with
29:    **Account → Workers AI → Read**… chat completions require write-style
30:    inference scope on some plans; if calls 403, widen to the template).
31: 3. Copy the token once. It cannot be viewed again.
32: 
33: Never paste the token into chat, git, `wrangler.jsonc`, or `.env.example`.
34: Only into host environment settings.
35: 
36: ## 3. Set the environment where the server runs
37: 
38: All three are needed for Workers AI (or set `XAI_API_KEY` instead to use xAI):
39: 
40: | Variable | Value |
41: | --- | --- |
42: | `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | `8501d3eeac693b7ada630058ee5e081a` |
43: | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | the token from step 2 |
44: | `WORKERS_AI_MODEL` | optional, default `@cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast` |
45: 
46: - **Local:** copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill the three in.
47: - **Vercel:** Project → Settings → Environment Variables → add all three
48:   (all environments), then redeploy.
49: - **Docker:** put them in the host `.env` read by `docker-compose.yml`.
50: 
51: With neither Cloudflare nor xAI set, the staff answer that they are
52: unavailable — everything else still works.
53: 
54: ## 4. Verify
55: 
56: ```sh
57: npm run cf:check            # offline wiring report, secrets hidden
58: curl http://localhost:8080/api/ai/status   # live probe after `npm run dev`
59: ```
60: 
61: Expect `"provider": "workers-ai"`. Then send the office chat a question;
62: a model-backed reply (not "unavailable") confirms end-to-end inference.
63: 
64: ## 5. Secret hygiene (required)
65: 
66: A `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN` was previously committed in `wrangler.jsonc` and has
67: been removed. Treat it as exposed:
68: 
69: 1. Generate a fresh one: `openssl rand -base64 32`.
70: 2. Set it in host env, complete founder setup at `/office`, then **remove
71:    the variable and redeploy** (sign-up closes once a founder exists).
72: 3. Rotate the Cloudflare API token too if it ever shared a screen, chat log,
73:    or commit with the old value.
74: 
75: ## Troubleshooting
76: 
77: | Symptom | Cause / fix |
78: | --- | --- |
79: | `cf:check` says `MALFORMED` | Whitespace or truncated id; must be exactly 32 hex chars. |
80: | Status probe says `none` | Token or id missing on the *server* host; `export` locally is not enough. |
81: | Model 401/403 | Token lacks Workers AI scope, or belongs to another account. |
82: | Model 429/5xx | The app retries once, then reports "did not answer in time". Wait and retry. |
83: | `AI_PROVIDER=xai` set | Forces xAI even when Cloudflare is configured; unset it to prefer Workers AI. |

1: # Autonomy roadmap — verified state and the ordered increments
2: 
3: Status as of 2026-10-24. Everything in "verified" was checked against the real
4: systems on that date: the test suite ran green, the Neon database answered,
5: and the production site was probed over HTTPS. Nothing here is aspirational
6: wording — each claim names the check that proved it.
7: 
8: ## Verified running today
9: 
10: | System                                                                                      | Evidence                                                                                | Result                                                                                                              |
11: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
12: | Autonomy engine (nine agents, durable queue, founder gates, delegation, hash-chained audit) | `npm test` + `npm run verify:office`                                                    | 243/243 checks passed, no mocks, no sample data                                                                     |
13: | Neon database                                                                               | connectivity check against the pooled host                                              | PostgreSQL 18.6 answered; `scripts/migrate.mjs` reports up to date — 16 migrations applied                          |
14: | Production site                                                                             | `GET https://www.vantage-ars.co.za/` and `/api/health`                                  | both 200; health reports `state: operational`, records and decision-record integrity ok                             |
15: | Cron endpoint guard                                                                         | `GET /api/cron/floor` without a bearer token                                            | 401 Unauthorized — the endpoint only acts with `CRON_SECRET`                                                        |
16: | Self-nudge                                                                                  | `src/routes/api/health.ts`, `src/routes/api/site-signal.ts`                             | both call `nudgeScheduler`, so any health probe or real page view starts a catch-up tick when the last one is stale |
17: | GitHub Actions heartbeat                                                                    | `.github/workflows/office-scheduler.yml`                                                | every 10 minutes, `CRON_SECRET` as a repository secret, loud errors on 401/404/500                                  |
18: | Docker + systemd paths                                                                      | `docker-compose.yml` (scheduler sidecar), `deploy/systemd/` (service + 10-minute timer) | committed; no external monitor needed on those targets                                                              |
19: | Cloudflare Worker (D1 + Workers AI + durable workflows, crons every 15 min)                 | `workers/vantage-ars/wrangler.toml`                                                     | config is real and account-bound; deploys via `deploy-vantage-ars.yml`                                              |
20: 
21: ## The increments, in order
22: 
23: ### 1. The four switches (no code — configuration only)
24: 
25: 1. Host environment: `DATABASE_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`,
26:    `AUTONOMY=on`, `CRON_SECRET`, `FOUNDER_EMAIL`. Generate the two secrets
27:    with `scripts/setup-autonomy.sh` or `openssl rand -base64 32` /
28:    `openssl rand -hex 32`.
29: 2. GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions: `CRON_SECRET`, the
30:    same value as the host's.
31: 3. Once: `FOUNDER_SETUP_TOKEN`, open `/office`, create the founder account,
32:    remove the token, redeploy.
33: 4. In-app, the last autonomy switch: `/office/delegations` — save a standing
34:    delegation. With none, every cost, customer win/loss and handoff stops at
35:    the founder gate. That is by design.
36: 
37: ### 2. Model-driven reasoning for the agents (needs one valid Cloudflare token)
38: 
39: The app's provider layer (`src/lib/office/ai-provider.ts`) already speaks
40: Cloudflare Workers AI. What is missing is a token Cloudflare accepts.
41: 
42: - Tried on 2026-10-24, twice: `GET /user/tokens/verify` and
43:   `GET /accounts/<account_id>/tokens/verify` both returned
44:   `{"success":false,"errors":[{"code":1000,"message":"Invalid API Token"}]}`.
45:   The values tried are paste-prefixed strings, not dashboard-issued API tokens (a dashboard token carries no such prefix).
46: - TODO(founder): create a token at My Profile → API Tokens (no prefix) with
47:   Workers AI permissions, then set `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` +
48:   `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` on the host and run `npm run cf:check`. Every
49:   autonomous duty already runs without it — the agents decide from office
50:   records; the model only sharpens drafted text.
51: 
52: ### 3. Worker deploy (same token)
53: 
54: `git push` to `main` already triggers `.github/workflows/deploy-vantage-ars.yml`
55: for changes under `workers/vantage-ars/`. It needs `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` as a
56: repository secret with Workers Scripts + D1 edit permissions. The Worker then
57: serves from `*.workers.dev` (custom-domain attach is deliberately disabled
58: while Vercel serves the domain — see the comment in `wrangler.toml`).
59: 
60: ### 4. Reaching customers (optional, already built)
61: 
62: - Mail: verified implicit-TLS SMTP settings (`SMTP_*`). Legacy Gmail app-password settings remain a fallback.
63:   Without them every notice is still recorded in the office and read there.
64: - Founder notices on a second channel: `FOUNDER_WEBHOOK_URL` (Slack/Discord).
65: - Bank details on quotes/invoices: the five `PAYMENT_*` values, all or none.
66: 
67: ### 5. Hardening
68: 
69: - The circuit breaker tells the founder once, by the same mail and webhook path
70:   as every other office alert, on the tick that crosses the failure limit. A
71:   clean recovery sends one resume notice. It does not repeat every ten minutes.
72: - The daily briefing is already mailed from the books. A second weekly digest
73:   would repeat it.
74: - `/api/health` remains the public heartbeat. The ten-minute GitHub scheduler
75:   is the monitor.
76: 
77: ## The honest boundary
78: 
79: The code is not the bottleneck. Every autonomous behaviour the roadmap needs —
80: queue, cadences, gates, delegation, audit, self-halt, self-recovery, catch-up
81: ticks — is implemented and proven by 243 checks. What stands between here and
82: an unattended office is four configuration switches and one valid Cloudflare
83: token.

- Complete and validate the Hugging Face provider configuration, then commit all changes.

- Aim for complete autonomy and use free models.
- Preserve founder-governed business-action boundaries.
- Commit all changes when completed.

- Use Hugging Face’s OpenAI-compatible chat-completions router and require a token when Hugging Face is explicitly selected.

- Describe Hugging Face free-tier credits and availability as limited, not guaranteed unlimited.

## Objective
- Improve Vantage-ARS toward an advanced autonomous AI-run business using free models, building on the existing project.
- Commit all completed changes.

## Requirements
- Aim for complete autonomy and use free models.
- Preserve founder-governed business-action boundaries.
- Commit all changes when completed.

## Decisions
- Use Hugging Face’s OpenAI-compatible chat-completions router; require a token when Hugging Face is explicitly selected.
- Do not silently switch providers if Hugging Face is explicitly selected but unavailable.
- Describe Hugging Face free-tier credits and availability as limited, not guaranteed unlimited.

## Work State
### Completed
- Updated the app provider resolver/tests for the Hugging Face router, default model `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`, token requirement, and explicit-provider behavior.
- Updated `.env.example`, conditional authorization headers in `src/lib/office/ai.server.ts`, readiness reporting in `src/routes/api/ai/status.ts`, and `scripts/cloudflare-check.mjs`.
- Added Hugging Face token/default/fallback tests to `scripts/cloudflare-check.test.mjs`.
- Updated Hugging Face guidance in `docs/next-steps.md` and `docs/autonomy-roadmap.md`.

### Active
- Review the full diff, run available validation, and commit all changes.

### Blocked
- Dependencies are missing (`node_modules` absent); earlier `npm run typecheck` failed with `sh: 1: tsc: not found`. Full test/typecheck/lint validation has not run.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `git status` and review the complete diff, including the latest documentation and checker test edits.
2. Run focused tests and available checks; if appropriate, install dependencies and run `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, and lint.
3. Fix any issues, then commit all completed changes.

## Relevant Files
- `src/lib/office/ai-provider.ts`: provider selection and Hugging Face router configuration.
- `src/lib/office/ai-provider.test.ts`: provider selection tests.
- `src/lib/office/ai.server.ts`: model requests and conditional authorization.
- `src/routes/api/ai/status.ts`: provider readiness endpoint.
- `scripts/cloudflare-check.mjs`: offline provider configuration checker.
- `scripts/cloudflare-check.test.mjs`: checker tests, including Hugging Face behavior.
- `docs/next-steps.md`: provider setup guidance.
- `docs/autonomy-roadmap.md`: current autonomy/provider status.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; modified files include `.env.example`, the provider/checker code and tests, `src/lib/office/ai.server.ts`, `src/routes/api/ai/status.ts`, and both documentation files.
- `scripts/cloudflare-check.mjs` now treats explicitly selected Hugging Face without a token as `none`, uses `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` by default, and does not consider `HUGGINGFACE_MODEL` alone sufficient.
